issues.legal_issue: A re-grant of an abolished impartible service estate to the eldest son as representative of the family group does not make the estate his personal property and leaves the other heirs entitled to their shares under their applicable law of inheritance.
material_facts: The agricultural properties had been impartible Inams that devolved on the eldest son by primogeniture because services to the ruler were rendered through him.
After abolition of the Inams, the properties were re-granted to the eldest son as Watandar.
The other children claimed their inheritance shares, and the eldest son argued that the re-granted properties were his personal property.

The court found no basis to distinguish the principles applied in Nagesh Bisto Desai and Annasaheb Bapusaheb Patil merely because the heirs were Muslim; it held that the heirs could claim shares under Shariat law.
issues.conclusion: The re-grant did not make the properties the eldest son's personal estate; the other heirs were entitled to their respective shares under Shariat law.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the principle in Nagesh Bisto Desai and Annasaheb Bapusaheb Patil that when an impartible service estate is abolished and re-granted to its holder, the former impartibility ends and the family group may claim shares. It found no reason to exclude Muslim heirs from that principle and held that their shares were determined under Shariat law. The abolition and re-grant occurred under the Bombay Merged Territories Miscellaneous Alienations Abolition Act, 1955.

rule.if: abolition_regrant_dispute and impartible_service_estate and estate_held_for_family_group and regrant_to_family_representative and regrant_ended_impartibility

predicates.abolition_regrant_dispute: The dispute concerns an estate that was abolished as a tenure and subsequently re-granted.
predicates.impartible_service_estate: The estate was impartible and services associated with it were rendered through the eldest family member.
predicates.estate_held_for_family_group: The eldest holder represented a group of family members in holding the estate.
predicates.regrant_to_family_representative: The estate was re-granted to the family member who had represented the group.
predicates.regrant_ended_impartibility: The re-grant ended the estate's former impartible character.

issues.definition: When an abolished impartible service estate held through a family representative is re-granted to that representative and the re-grant ends impartibility, the former heirs are entitled to inheritance shares.

issues.legal_issue: A claim of adverse possession against other heirs is not established when the claimant pleads the duration of exclusive possession but fails to plead acts showing when that possession became hostile and notorious to the exclusion of the other heirs.
material_facts: The claimant asserted a duration of exclusive possession of the house against the other heirs.
The written statement did not identify an overt act or a point in time from which possession became hostile and notorious to the other heirs' exclusion.
Municipal register entries were offered as evidence, but the court held that evidence could not substitute for the necessary pleadings.
The High Court reversed the lower courts' finding for the claimant, and the Supreme Court found no reason to interfere with that reversal.
issues.conclusion: The adverse-possession claim failed because the pleadings did not state the hostile and notorious acts on which it depended, and the High Court's reversal was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: A claimant relying on adverse possession must plead facts showing that possession became hostile and notorious, openly and to the exclusion of the other heirs, from an identifiable point in time. Evidence, including municipal register entries, cannot substitute for pleadings, which form the foundation of a litigant's claim. The court cited no provision or earlier case for this principle.

rule.if: adverse_possession_title_dispute and claim_against_coheirs and exclusive_possession_duration_pleaded and pleading_omits_hostile_overt_acts

predicates.adverse_possession_title_dispute: The proceeding concerns a claim to establish title by adverse possession.
predicates.claim_against_coheirs: The claimant asserts adverse possession against other heirs to the property.
predicates.exclusive_possession_duration_pleaded: The claimant pleads how long the claimant remained in exclusive possession.
predicates.pleading_omits_hostile_overt_acts: The claimant's pleading does not identify acts showing when possession became hostile and notorious to the other heirs' exclusion.

issues.definition: In a title dispute involving a claim against coheirs, pleading the duration of exclusive possession without hostile overt acts does not establish adverse possession.
